title: 450. Custer's Last Stand: Death in the Black Hills (Part 5)

sentences.en: If I were an Indian, I often think that I would greatly prefer to cast my lot among those of my people
sentences.zh: 我常想，如果我是印第安人，我宁愿选择与我的族人站在一起，

sentences.en: who adhere to the free open plains, rather than submit to the confined limits of a reservation.
sentences.zh: 那些坚守在自由开阔平原上的人，也不愿屈服于保留地那狭小的界限。

sentences.en: There would be the recipient of the blessed benefits of civilization, with its vices thrown in without stint or measure.
sentences.zh: 在那里，人们可以享受到文明带来的福祉，同时也毫无保留地承受着文明的恶习。

sentences.en: He is neither a luxury nor necessary of life.
sentences.zh: 对他而言，文明既非奢侈品，也非必需品。

sentences.en: He can hunt, roam, and camp when and wheresoever he pleases.
sentences.zh: 他可以在任何他想去的地方，随时狩猎、漫游和露营。

sentences.en: Provided always that in so doing he does not run contrary to the requirements of civilization in its advancing tread.
sentences.zh: 前提是，他这样做不能违背文明前进的步伐所提出的要求。

sentences.en: When the soil which he has claimed and hunted over for so long a time is demanded by this to him, insatiable monster, there is no appeal.
sentences.zh: 当他长期占据并狩猎的土地被这头对他而言贪得无厌的怪兽索要时，他没有任何申诉的余地。

sentences.en: He must yield, or like the car of Juggernaut, it will roll mercilessly over him, destroying as it advances.
sentences.zh: 他必须屈服，否则这头“札格纳特”战车就会无情地碾过他，所到之处尽皆毁灭。

sentences.en: Destiny seems to have so willed it, and the world looks on and nods its approval.
sentences.zh: 命运似乎就是这样安排的，而世界只是冷眼旁观，点头默许。

sentences.en: The way he sort of reconciles his genuine, I think, interest and respect sort of in and for these people with his belief that, you know, they do have to be swept aside.

sentences.en: It's that he says they can never be civilized.
sentences.zh: 就是他说他们永远无法被文明化。

sentences.zh: 大自然注定印第安人处于野蛮状态。

sentences.en: Every instinct, every impulse of his soul inclines him to it.
sentences.zh: 他灵魂中的每一个本能、每一个冲动都倾向于此。

sentences.en: He cannot be himself and be civilized.
sentences.zh: 他无法在保持自我的同时被文明化。

sentences.en: He must fade away and die.
sentences.zh: 他必须消亡。

sentences.en: Custer really, I think he really believes that.
sentences.zh: 卡斯特真的，我认为他真的相信这一点。

sentences.en: That's not just a fig leaf.
sentences.zh: 那不仅仅是一个遮羞布。

sentences.en: He thinks this is the law of nature and of science, that this is the fate of the plains Indians.
sentences.zh: 他认为这是自然法则和科学规律，这就是平原印第安人的命运。

sentences.en: I mean, I wonder, maybe I'm overemphasizing it because I am interested in the subject,

sentences.en: It's casting the idea that human civilizations follow the same route, that just as dinosaurs have been superseded by mammals, so Indians, as Custer would put it,
sentences.zh: 这让人联想到人类文明也遵循同样的路线，正如恐龙被哺乳动物取代一样，印第安人，用卡斯特的话说，

sentences.en: must be superseded by the white man.
sentences.zh: 也必须被白人取代。

sentences.en: I don't think that's too fanciful at all, Tom.
sentences.zh: 我不认为这太异想天开了，汤姆。

sentences.zh: 我认为卡斯特显然是他那个时代的人。

sentences.en: but they are like a species that is basically doomed by the laws of nature and whatnot.
sentences.zh: 但他们就像一个基本上被自然法则等注定要灭亡的物种。

sentences.en: I think that, as you say, the fact that it's taking place in this landscape with layers upon layers of deep, deep history, yeah,

sentences.zh: 显然我认为这其中一定存在某种间接的心理联系。

sentences.en: I mean, it's also that the Native Americans themselves are very familiar with fossils and tell all kinds of stories about them, say stories of thunderbirds and so on.

sentences.en: And now that the paleontologists are coming out with their chisels and saying, actually, you know, this was from the Jurassic period or whatever.

sentences.en: So in the spring of 1873, Custer ends up in the Dakota Territory, a place called Fort Abraham Lincoln on the Missouri River opposite the town of Bismarck.

sentences.en: And just to reiterate, Dakota is, I mean, it's just another pronunciation of Lakota.
sentences.zh: 重申一下，达科他，我的意思是，这只是拉科塔的另一种发音。

sentences.en: Yeah.

sentences.en: And here, Custer, who's actually pretty miserable in all the accounts of him from other soldiers, because he hates kind of being a pen pushing general.
sentences.zh: 在这里，卡斯特，在其他士兵对他的描述中，他其实过得很痛苦，因为他讨厌当一个只会写写画画的将军。

sentences.en: He hates all that and he's very bad at it.
sentences.zh: 他讨厌这一切，而且他很不擅长。

sentences.en: But he gets a chance for a bit of action because the Northern Pacific Railway is planning to come through this territory.
sentences.zh: 但他获得了一次行动的机会，因为北太平洋铁路计划穿过这片领土。

sentences.en: Now, the Northern Pacific is the perfect symbol of the modernity against which people set the Plains Indians,

sentences.en: because it is the project of America's first really big investment banker, a guy called Jay Cook, who had basically bankrolled the Union war effort, the North, in the Civil War.
sentences.zh: 因为它是美国第一位真正的大投资银行家杰伊·库克的项目，他基本上资助了内战中联邦的战争努力。

sentences.en: He is by far the best known, at this point, financier in America.
sentences.zh: 在当时，他是美国最著名的金融家。

sentences.en: It's his railroad.

sentences.en: Yeah.

sentences.en: So, from 1872 to 1874, non-Indian hunters on the Southern Plains alone killed more than 3 million bison.
sentences.zh: 所以，从1872年到1874年，仅在南部平原，非印第安猎人就杀死了超过300万头野牛。

sentences.en: By the mid-1870s, bison were nearly extinct on the Central Plains.
sentences.zh: 到19世纪70年代中期，野牛在中部平原几乎灭绝了。

sentences.en: Yeah.

sentences.en: And it's obvious to everyone that they're not going to be around for long.

sentences.en: So, General Sheridan, General Sherman, in their correspondence, they say again and again, here we go, let them kill and skin until the buffalo are exterminated.

sentences.en: And that word exterminated, which to us has such terrifying connotations, they use that a lot, not talking not just of the bison, but of the Plains Indians.

sentences.en: They equate the two.
sentences.zh: 他们将两者等同起来。

sentences.en: So, Sherman, the white public are clamorous for extermination, which is easier said than done.

sentences.en: But he says, we're not moved by mere human sentiments.
sentences.zh: 但他又说，我们不会被单纯的人类情感所动摇。

sentences.en: Now, he then goes on to say, I'm very happy to exterminate Indians who send out thieving,
sentences.zh: 接着他又说，我很乐意消灭那些派出偷窃、

sentences.en: But I think they have, as Custer does, an assumption that actually extermination is the natural end point and that what they are doing is they are just smoothing that process, but

sentences.zh: 尽可能人道地进行。

sentences.en: That's how they think of it.
sentences.zh: 他们就是这么想的。

sentences.en: It's very chilling because, of course, this scientific approach to eradicating entire peoples is going to blow back into Europe.
sentences.zh: 这非常令人不寒而栗，因为当然，这种根除整个民族的科学方法最终会反噬欧洲。

sentences.en: Of course.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But they will go back to Europe, you know, and we know what happens there.
sentences.zh: 但你知道，他们会回到欧洲，我们也知道那里会发生什么。

sentences.en: Of course.

sentences.en: So in the early days of August, Bloody Knife says to Custer, I think we're being followed.
sentences.zh: 所以在8月初，“血刀”对卡斯特说，我想我们被跟踪了。

sentences.en: You know, I've seen kind of signs.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我看到了一些迹象。

sentences.en: I don't know what a scout sees, but anyway, he's seen them.
sentences.zh: 我不知道侦察兵看到了什么，但总之，他看到了。

sentences.en: Trails, I think.
sentences.zh: 我想是足迹。

sentences.en: Trails and people preparing to ambush us.
sentences.zh: 足迹，还有人准备伏击我们。

sentences.en: And early on the 4th of August, this is exactly what happens.
sentences.zh: 8月4日一早，情况果然如此。

sentences.en: The Lakota, they try to do a Fetterman massacre maneuver to lure Custer out.
sentences.zh: 拉科塔人试图用费特曼大屠杀那样的战术来诱骗卡斯特出来。

sentences.en: And to cut a sort of very long story short, what actually happens is that Custer and his men and about 90 men end up being trapped by three times as many Lakota in these woods by
sentences.zh: 长话短说，实际情况是卡斯特和他的大约90名部下，最终被三倍于己的拉科塔人困在了黄石河边的树林里。

sentences.en: the Yellowstone River.
sentences.zh: 黄石河。

sentences.en: And there are Lakota and their Cheyenne allies kind of riding around them.
sentences.zh: 拉科塔人和他们的夏延盟友在他们周围骑马盘旋。

sentences.en: They try and burn them out by setting fire to the grass.
sentences.zh: 他们试图通过点燃草地把他们烧出来。

sentences.en: And Custer, now, I think this is important because it's really important, I think, to question the idea that Custer is just a terrible commander who's really reckless.
sentences.zh: 现在，我觉得这一点很重要，因为质疑“卡斯特只是一个鲁莽且糟糕的指挥官”这一观点非常重要。

sentences.en: His instinct is always to do the sort of mad swashbuckling gamble.
sentences.zh: 他的本能总是去做那种疯狂的、孤注一掷的赌博。

sentences.en: It kind of is though, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 但事实确实如此，不是吗？

sentences.en: But here he doesn't do that at all.
sentences.zh: 但在这里，他完全没有那样做。

sentences.en: He keeps his men together.
sentences.zh: 他让部下保持集结。

sentences.en: He deploys them in a defensive line.
sentences.zh: 他部署了防线。

sentences.en: He keeps order and discipline.
sentences.zh: 他保持了秩序和纪律。

sentences.en: He doesn't charge out.
sentences.zh: 他没有冲出去。

sentences.en: He says we won't fall for that.
sentences.zh: 他说我们不会上当。

sentences.en: They're trying to lure us out and to trap us.
sentences.zh: 他们想诱我们出去并困住我们。

sentences.en: Custer does really well here, Tom, I think.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，我觉得卡斯特在这里表现得非常好。

sentences.en: But his assumption is that the 7th Cavalry will always beat Native Americans.
sentences.zh: 但他预设的前提是第7骑兵团总能打败美洲原住民。

sentences.en: I mean, that's his guiding assumption.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是他的指导思想。

sentences.en: And in the event, that is going to be shown not necessarily to be true, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 但事实证明，这未必正确，不是吗？

sentences.en: Of course, yes.
sentences.zh: 当然，是的。

sentences.en: But the reason that he's kind of he's charging out, he's happy to venture into places where he may well be ambushed, where there may well be giant villages.
sentences.zh: 但他之所以冲出去，是因为他乐于冒险进入那些很可能被伏击、可能有巨大村庄的地方。

sentences.en: And he assumes that he will always have the beating of them.
sentences.zh: 他认为自己总能战胜他们。

sentences.en: I think that reflects a certain degree of swashbuckling confidence that in the event will come to seem misplaced.
sentences.zh: 我认为这反映了一种孤注一掷的自信，事后看来这种自信显得有些错位。

sentences.en: I take your point that he's never frightened because he always thinks they'll win.
sentences.zh: 我明白你的意思，他从不害怕，因为他总觉得他们会赢。

sentences.en: But I think in this case, I think you're being a tiny bit harsh on Custer because I think it's the Lakota here that have attacked him, not vice versa.
sentences.zh: 但我认为在这种情况下，你对卡斯特有点苛刻了，因为我认为是拉科塔人先攻击了他，而不是反过来。

sentences.en: Yeah, but I mean, he's kind of ridden into their territory.
sentences.zh: 是的，但我的意思是，他毕竟闯入了他们的领地。

sentences.en: He has, but he's under orders.
sentences.zh: 确实，但他是在执行命令。

sentences.en: He hasn't done it out of...
sentences.zh: 他不是出于……

sentences.en: Well, fine.
sentences.zh: 好吧，行。

sentences.en: But I mean, that's no skin off the Lakota nose.
sentences.zh: 但我的意思是，这对拉科塔人来说没什么损失。

sentences.en: No, OK, fair enough.
sentences.zh: 不，好吧，说得有道理。

sentences.en: Anyway, he does do well.
sentences.zh: 总之，他表现得确实不错。

sentences.en: You know, he does really well.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他表现得非常好。

sentences.en: Dominic, the other thing is the weaponry.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，还有一件事是武器装备。

sentences.en: I know that you love military hardware.
sentences.zh: 我知道你喜欢军事装备。

sentences.en: Can't get enough of that.
sentences.zh: 怎么看都不够。

sentences.en: The assumption that the Americans have rifles and the Indians have bows and arrows is very hardwired, isn't it, into the kind of the popular mythology of it?
sentences.zh: 美国人有步枪，印第安人有弓箭，这种假设已经深深植根于流行神话中了，不是吗？

sentences.en: It is.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: The Lakota actually have...
sentences.zh: 拉科塔人实际上有……

sentences.en: I mean, they're pretty well armed as well.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们也装备精良。

sentences.en: Yeah, they have rifles.
sentences.zh: 是的，他们有步枪。

sentences.en: The one problem the Lakota have is getting ammunition.
sentences.zh: 拉科塔人面临的一个问题是获取弹药。

sentences.en: Do you know who gave the Lakota their first rifles?
sentences.zh: 你知道是谁给了拉科塔人第一批步枪吗？

sentences.en: Make you feel very patriotic.
sentences.zh: 这会让你感到非常爱国。

sentences.en: Oh.
sentences.zh: 哦。

sentences.en: It was the British.
sentences.zh: 是英国人。

sentences.en: Really?
sentences.zh: 真的吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: For the War of 1812?
sentences.zh: 为了1812年战争？

sentences.en: Just before the outbreak of war.
sentences.zh: 就在战争爆发前夕。

sentences.en: So it was us.
sentences.zh: 所以是我们干的。

sentences.en: Well, that's good behaviour.
sentences.zh: 嗯，那真是“好行为”。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Oh, that's very pleasing.
sentences.zh: 哦，那真是太令人“高兴”了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And so Custer actually is often complaining about the fact that the state government is giving guns to the people that he's then having to go out and fight with.
sentences.zh: 所以卡斯特经常抱怨州政府给那些他不得不去战斗的人提供枪支。

sentences.en: Well, of course.
sentences.zh: 嗯，当然。

sentences.en: So if you take the offer of going to a reservation, what you want to get is you want supplies, you want blankets, you want food and all that.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你接受去保留地的提议，你想要的是补给、毯子、食物等等。

sentences.en: But what the Lakota are always asking the reservation agents and things for is they're saying, please, can we have some guns?
sentences.zh: 但拉科塔人总是向保留地代理人要求的是，请问能给我们一些枪吗？

sentences.en: And that's a real source of contention, actually.
sentences.zh: 这确实是一个真正的争论焦点。

sentences.en: They say, we want the guns to hunt the bison.
sentences.zh: 他们说，我们需要枪来猎杀野牛。

sentences.en: It's really important for us to be able to do it.
sentences.zh: 这对我们来说非常重要。

sentences.en: But of course, the Americans are often quite torn about this because why do we want to give them guns?
sentences.zh: 但当然，美国人对此往往很纠结，因为为什么要给他们枪呢？

sentences.en: Then they'll probably use them on us.
sentences.zh: 他们可能会用这些枪来对付我们。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So Custer in My Life on the Plains, I mean, he talks about the wise foresight and strong love of fair play which prevails in the Indian department, which seeing that its wars are
sentences.zh: 所以卡斯特在《我在平原上的生活》中，谈到了印第安事务部所盛行的“明智的远见”和“强烈的公平竞争精神”，该部门认为既然战争已经

sentences.en: determined to fight is equally determined that there shall be no advantage taken, but that the two sides shall be armed alike.
sentences.zh: 不可避免，那么双方都应该武装对等，不应占任何便宜。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So very kind of heavy sarcasm there.
sentences.zh: 所以这里有非常强烈的讽刺意味。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错，没错，没错。

sentences.en: He says the red man is not far behind his more civilised brother in the art of war.
sentences.zh: 他说红种人在战争艺术上并不落后于他那更文明的兄弟。

sentences.en: But I think there is an element of exaggeration there, isn't there?
sentences.zh: 但我认为其中有夸大的成分，不是吗？

sentences.en: A little bit.
sentences.zh: 有一点。

sentences.en: I mean, the guns that the Americans have are better quality.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，美国人拥有的枪支质量更好。

sentences.en: By and large, often they just have single shot carbines, though.
sentences.zh: 不过总的来说，他们通常只有单发卡宾枪。

sentences.en: So it's not like they're going, there's a big difference between the Americans at this point.
sentences.zh: 所以这不像……美国人在这一点上并没有太大的优势。

sentences.en: And let us say, if you think about the British in the Sudan or something, you know, mowing people down with their machine guns.
sentences.zh: 比如，想想英国人在苏丹等地，用机枪扫射人们。

sentences.en: This is absolutely not the case at this point on the Western frontier.
sentences.zh: 在西部边境的这个时期，情况绝对不是这样。

sentences.en: I mean, often Custer's men, their guns don't work.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，卡斯特部下的枪经常无法使用。

sentences.en: They explode in their faces.
sentences.zh: 它们会在他们脸上炸开。

sentences.en: The men themselves are terribly badly trained and don't know what they're doing.
sentences.zh: 士兵们本身训练极其糟糕，根本不知道自己在做什么。

sentences.en: All of which makes it weird and, I guess, expressive of the sense of dash and self-confidence that makes Custer such an effective performer up until he no longer is.
sentences.zh: 所有这些都显得很奇怪，我想，这表现出了一种冲劲和自信，使卡斯特成为了一名高效的指挥官，直到他不再是为止。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That he can kind of ride into battle and get his men to believe that they can do this.
sentences.zh: 他能冲进战场，让他的部下相信他们能做到这一点。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Because he does it again a few days later, the 11th of AuguSt.
sentences.zh: 因为几天后的8月11日，他又做了一次。

sentences.en: There's a Lakota attack.
sentences.zh: 发生了拉科塔人的袭击。

sentences.en: Like, again, Custer's men are cornered on the banks of the Yellowstone.
sentences.zh: 就像之前一样，卡斯特的部下被困在黄石河岸边。

sentences.en: Sitting Bull is watching this, by the way, from the bluffs across the river.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，坐牛（Sitting Bull）正从河对岸的悬崖上看着这一切。

sentences.en: So although Custer and Sitting Bull never actually, as it were, meet, this is the first time,
sentences.zh: 所以虽然卡斯特和坐牛实际上从未见过面，但这是第一次，

sentences.en: I guess, that they've been, if you're making a film, it's the first time they're in the same shot.
sentences.zh: 我想，如果是在拍电影，这是他们第一次出现在同一个镜头里。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.zh: 坐牛看到了“长发”（卡斯特的绰号）。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错，正是如此。

sentences.en: And the Lakota are taunting Custer's men.
sentences.zh: 拉科塔人在嘲讽卡斯特的部下。

sentences.en: Come out, come out.
sentences.zh: 出来，出来。

sentences.en: We're going to have those horses of yours at some stage.
sentences.zh: 我们迟早会得到你们的那些马。

sentences.en: You may as well cross and, like, have the fight and give them to us now.
sentences.zh: 你们不如现在就过河来打一仗，把马交给我们。

sentences.en: And Custer, again, Tom, I think, does well.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，我觉得卡斯特在这里又表现得很好。

sentences.en: He says, no, no, hold on, hold on.
sentences.zh: 他说，不，不，等等，等等。

sentences.en: Let's bide our time.
sentences.zh: 让我们静观其变。

sentences.en: Don't do anything rash.
sentences.zh: 不要做任何鲁莽的事。

sentences.en: All of this kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 诸如此类的话。

sentences.zh: 最后，在斯坦利的指挥下，一支救援部队抵达了，他指挥着这次远征，此时他已经完全改变了对卡斯特的看法，认为卡斯特

sentences.en: a great fellow.
sentences.zh: 是一个了不起的家伙。

sentences.zh: 接着卡斯特发起了那场伟大的“海尔姆深谷”式冲锋。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.zh: 他排好了阵型。

sentences.zh: 他头发飞扬。

sentences.zh: 他们奏响了那首曲子——《加里·欧文》，那是他们喜欢跳的一种爱尔兰吉格舞曲，然后他们就全冲了出去。

sentences.en: And it's very dramatic.
sentences.zh: 场面非常戏剧性。

sentences.en: The thing about Custer's charge is, as we said in the very first episode, he knows when to do it, but he does love a charge.
sentences.zh: 关于卡斯特的冲锋，正如我们在第一集里所说，他知道什么时候该冲锋，但他确实热爱冲锋。

sentences.en: He does indeed.
sentences.zh: 他确实如此。

sentences.en: It works very well.
sentences.zh: 效果非常好。

sentences.zh: 拉科塔人逃跑了。

sentences.en: Everybody says Custer has, you know, he's redeemed himself.
sentences.zh: 大家都说卡斯特，你知道的，他实现了自我救赎。

sentences.en: The expedition has been a success, a relative success.
sentences.zh: 这次远征取得了成功，相对的成功。

sentences.zh: 谢里丹写信给他，说干得好。

sentences.en: Brilliant.

sentences.en: Everyone thinks you're great.
sentences.zh: 大家都觉得你很了不起。

sentences.zh: 报纸上说美国的光荣之子回来了。

sentences.en: And now, Dominic, we're in 1873.
sentences.zh: 现在，多米尼克，我们来到了1873年。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: A chance is approaching for him to have another crack.
sentences.zh: 他即将迎来再次尝试的机会。

sentences.en: There is.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: There is another chance.
sentences.zh: 还有另一个机会。

sentences.en: So, just to give people a bit of context on this.
sentences.zh: 那么，为了让大家了解一下背景。

sentences.en: The big thing that 1873 is well known for in American history is a tremendous stock market crash.
sentences.zh: 1873年在美国历史上最出名的事情就是一场巨大的股市崩盘。

sentences.en: So, it's called the Panic of 1873.
sentences.zh: 所以，它被称为1873年大恐慌。

sentences.en: People used to call this, by the way, the Great Depression.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，人们过去常称之为“大萧条”。

sentences.en: Before the Great Depression happened.
sentences.zh: 在大萧条发生之前。

sentences.en: And it's railroads that crash, including Northern Pacific.
sentences.zh: 崩盘的是铁路，包括北太平洋铁路。

sentences.en: And it's the empire of this guy, Jay Cook, who we talked about in the first half, who was the great kind of railroad banker and railroad financier.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们在上半部分提到的杰伊·库克的帝国，他是那位伟大的铁路银行家和铁路金融家。

sentences.en: The impact of this crash is absolutely seismic.
sentences.zh: 这次崩盘的影响绝对是地震级的。

sentences.en: It's completely forgotten now because nobody studies the history of the 1870s and 1880s, really.
sentences.zh: 现在它被完全遗忘了，因为真的没人研究19世纪70年代和80年代的历史。

sentences.en: But, you know, to give you an example, a quarter of all the people in New York City lost their jobs in the next few months after this crash in September 1873.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，举个例子，在1873年9月这次崩盘后的几个月里，纽约市四分之一的人失业了。

sentences.en: And why this matters is it puts enormous pressure on the frontier because it means that there are a lot of people whose lives in the big cities of the East Coast have been destroyed
sentences.zh: 这之所以重要，是因为它给边疆带来了巨大的压力，因为这意味着许多人在东海岸大城市的生活被摧毁了，

sentences.en: and are desperate to start new lives as miners, as, you know, homesteaders, as farmers, in what they are beginning to see.
sentences.zh: 他们迫切希望作为矿工、定居者、农民，在他们开始看到的地方开启新的生活。

sentences.en: Having people have dismissed the Great Plains for decades.
sentences.zh: 尽管人们几十年来一直不看好大平原。

sentences.en: But now people are sort of saying, well, maybe this is the promised land.
sentences.zh: 但现在人们开始说，嗯，也许这就是应许之地。

sentences.en: Maybe we can start new lives out here.
sentences.zh: 也许我们可以在这里开始新的生活。

sentences.en: Now, the fact that there are some people there already.
sentences.zh: 现在，事实上那里已经有一些人了。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's the relevance.
sentences.zh: 是的，这就是关联所在。

sentences.en: Who cares about that?
sentences.zh: 谁在乎那个？

sentences.en: Well, exactly.
sentences.zh: 嗯，确实。

sentences.en: And also the prospect of finding gold.
sentences.zh: 还有发现黄金的前景。

sentences.en: Oh, yeah.
sentences.zh: 哦，是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I mean, it's all very well setting up a farm.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，开个农场固然很好。

sentences.en: Yes, of course.
sentences.zh: 是的，当然。

sentences.en: But if you can go and find a large lump of gold, that's even better.
sentences.zh: 但如果你能去找到一大块金子，那就更好了。

sentences.en: Because if you're 40 in 1873, pretty much all your life, certainly all your life that you can remember, you've grown up in a world of gold rushes.
sentences.zh: 因为如果你在1873年时40岁，你几乎一生，至少是你记得的所有时间里，都是在淘金热的世界中长大的。

sentences.en: California, Colorado, there's been talk of gold in Oregon, all of these kinds of places.
sentences.zh: 加利福尼亚、科罗拉多，还有关于俄勒冈等地有黄金的传闻。

sentences.en: So you dream of a new gold rush where you can be rich overnight as people were in the California gold rush in the late 1840s and 1850s.
sentences.zh: 所以你梦想着一场新的淘金热，可以像19世纪40年代末和50年代加州淘金热时期的人们那样一夜暴富。

sentences.en: So that's hanging over this whole thing.
sentences.zh: 所以这笼罩着整件事。

sentences.en: You know, maybe the Great Plains have these amazing untapped resources.
sentences.zh: 你知道，也许大平原拥有这些惊人的未开发资源。

sentences.en: And there's one place, isn't there, in particular, that it's thought that there might be gold.
sentences.zh: 而且有一个地方，不是吗，特别被认为可能有黄金。

sentences.en: And this is a place called the Black Hills.
sentences.zh: 这就是一个叫黑山的地方。

sentences.en: The Black Hills.
sentences.zh: 黑山。

sentences.en: The reason they end up in the Black Hills, first of all, is actually because Sheridan wants a fort there.
sentences.zh: 他们最终进入黑山的原因，首先实际上是因为谢里丹想在那里建一座堡垒。

sentences.en: So the Black Hills are just outside the Great Sioux Reservation.
sentences.zh: 所以黑山就在大苏族保留地外面。

sentences.en: People may remember that in the last episode, well, when we talked about the deal that had been done with Red Cloud, the American government had given Lakota this big reservation,
sentences.zh: 大家可能还记得上一集，当我们谈到与红云达成的协议时，美国政府给了拉科塔人这个大保留地，

sentences.en: the Great Sioux Reservation, covering much of South Dakota.
sentences.zh: 大苏族保留地，覆盖了南达科他州的大部分地区。

sentences.en: But they said that all the land, basically to the west of it, was what was called unceded Indian territory, which is a kind of gray area.
sentences.zh: 但他们说，基本上西边的所有土地都是所谓的“未割让印第安领土”，这是一种灰色地带。

sentences.en: You know, the army can kind of go in, but they need to get permission.
sentences.zh: 你知道，军队可以进去，但他们需要获得许可。

sentences.en: Is it Indian?
sentences.zh: 那是印第安人的吗？

sentences.en: Is it American?
sentences.zh: 那是美国的吗？

sentences.en: Anyway, Sheridan wants to build a fort there.
sentences.zh: 总之，谢里丹想在那里建一座堡垒。

sentences.en: He doesn't like the fact that Sitting Bull and the non-treaty Indians, as they're called,
sentences.zh: 他不喜欢坐牛和那些所谓的“非条约印第安人”，

sentences.en: are kind of roaming around and are a little bit kind of disputatious and stuff and are fighting the crows and stuff.
sentences.zh: 到处游荡，有点好斗，还在和克罗人打仗之类的。

sentences.en: He wants to kind of sort this out and regularize it.
sentences.zh: 他想把这件事解决并规范化。

sentences.en: He says, I'd really like a fort in the Black Hills or just right next to the Black Hills.
sentences.zh: 他说，我真的很想在黑山或紧挨着黑山的地方建一座堡垒。

sentences.en: Now, the Black Hills, the Paha Sapa, as they're called, everybody thinks they're sacred to the Lakota.
sentences.zh: 现在，黑山，也就是所谓的“帕哈萨帕”，大家都认为它是拉科塔人的圣地。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So I had always thought that.
sentences.zh: 所以我一直也是这么想的。

sentences.en: Yeah, I did too.
sentences.zh: 是的，我也是。

sentences.en: I'd always assumed this.
sentences.zh: 我一直以为是这样。

sentences.en: I mean, this is the kind of, you know, the timeless spirit world of the Lakota kind of stuff that I had completely bought into.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这就像是那种，你知道，拉科塔人永恒的精神世界之类的东西，我完全相信了。

sentences.en: I mean, basically, they've been there three or four decades, something like that, and they've nicked them off.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，基本上，他们在那儿待了三四十年，差不多就是这样，而且是从别人手里抢来的。

sentences.en: Is it the Crow or the Cheyenne?
sentences.zh: 是克罗人还是夏延人？

sentences.en: I can't remember.
sentences.zh: 我不记得了。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: They'd fought for them.
sentences.zh: 他们为之战斗过。

sentences.en: They're actually more sacred.
sentences.zh: 它们实际上更神圣。

sentences.en: They are sacred to the Cheyenne.
sentences.zh: 它们对夏延人来说是神圣的。

sentences.en: They are sacred to the Cheyenne, aren't they?
sentences.zh: 它们对夏延人来说是神圣的，不是吗？

sentences.en: But not really to the Lakota.
sentences.zh: 但对拉科塔人来说其实不然。

sentences.en: The issue for the Lakota is, A, we've conquered them.
sentences.zh: 对拉科塔人来说，问题在于：第一，我们征服了它们。

sentences.en: They're ours.
sentences.zh: 它们是我们的。

sentences.en: It's ours.
sentences.zh: 它是我们的。

sentences.en: And I mean, the Lakota would say, hold on, that's how the United States thinks.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，拉科塔人会说，等等，美国人也是这么想的。

sentences.en: Yeah, of course.
sentences.zh: 是的，当然。

sentences.en: They think that when they conquer something, it's theirs.
sentences.zh: 他们认为当他们征服了某样东西，它就是他们的。

sentences.en: This is our thing.
sentences.zh: 这是我们的东西。

sentences.en: We should keep it.
sentences.zh: 我们应该保留它。

sentences.en: That they'd only conquered it a few decades before.
sentences.zh: 他们只是在几十年前才征服了它。

sentences.en: That's the thing.
sentences.zh: 就是这样。

sentences.en: Of course they had.
sentences.zh: 他们当然是这样。

sentences.en: And they would reasonably say, I mean, that's true of the United States.
sentences.zh: 而且他们会合理地说，我的意思是，美国也是如此。

sentences.en: Yeah, I'm sure.
sentences.zh: 是的，我肯定。

sentences.en: But it's not primordially since the beginning of time, since, you know, the Great Spirit gave to them kind of stuff.
sentences.zh: 但它并不是从时间之初，从你知道的，大灵赐予他们那种东西开始就原始存在的。

sentences.en: No, totally.
sentences.zh: 不，完全不是。

sentences.en: So everybody who thinks, you know, these were men and women of the earth.
sentences.zh: 所以那些认为他们是大地之子的人，

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Their timeless spirituality was rooted in the Black Hills.
sentences.zh: 他们永恒的灵性根植于黑山。

sentences.en: That's tosh and rubbish.
sentences.zh: 那是胡说八道。

sentences.en: And what they really want it for is it's very, very rich in buffalo.
sentences.zh: 他们真正想要它的原因是那里盛产野牛。

sentences.en: So there are kind of sheltered meadows where the buffalo can kind of graze.
sentences.zh: 所以那里有一些避风的草地，野牛可以在那里吃草。

sentences.en: But there are also loads of pine trees, which they use for their kind of poles and their lodges and stuff.
sentences.zh: 但那里也有大量的松树，他们用这些松树来做杆子、搭建棚屋之类的东西。

sentences.en: That sounds lovely.
sentences.zh: 听起来很不错。

sentences.en: It's brilliant for them.
sentences.zh: 这对他们来说太棒了。

sentences.en: Tyrannosaurs as well.
sentences.zh: 还有暴龙。

sentences.en: Tyrannosaur skeletons.
sentences.zh: 暴龙的骨架。

sentences.en: Are there good dinosaurs in the Black Hills, Tom?
sentences.zh: 汤姆，黑山里有好的恐龙化石吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, really good.
sentences.zh: 有，非常好的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Wonderful.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: So the Lakota are very displeased at any talk of the Black Hills being taken from them.
sentences.zh: 所以拉科塔人对任何关于从他们手中夺走黑山的言论都感到非常不满。

sentences.en: And of course, Sheridan says he needs to send out a survey mission.
sentences.zh: 当然，谢里丹说他需要派出一支勘测队。

sentences.en: Where are we going to put the fort?
sentences.zh: 我们要把堡垒建在哪里呢？

sentences.en: And the person he sends out is Custer.
sentences.zh: 而他派去的人就是卡斯特。

sentences.en: Custer goes with 10 companies, rather, of the 7th Cavalry.
sentences.zh: 卡斯特带着第七骑兵团的十个连出发了。

sentences.en: They've got Gatling guns.
sentences.zh: 他们有加特林机枪。

sentences.en: They have scouts.
sentences.zh: 他们有侦察兵。

sentences.en: They have scientists.
sentences.zh: 他们有科学家。

sentences.en: They have geologists, Tom.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，他们还有地质学家。

sentences.en: They have fossil hunters.
sentences.zh: 他们有化石猎人。

sentences.en: Custer's and President Grant's son, Fred, goes along, too, because he thinks this sounds brilliant.
sentences.zh: 卡斯特和格兰特总统的儿子弗雷德也随行，因为他觉得这听起来棒极了。

sentences.en: You know, what a great laugh this will be, going to the Black Hills.
sentences.zh: 你知道，去黑山探险该是多么有趣的一件事啊。

sentences.en: And loads of newspapermen go.
sentences.zh: 还有一大群报社记者随行。

sentences.en: And at this point, Custer's activities in the West have become a great media sensation.
sentences.zh: 此时，卡斯特在西部的活动已经成了媒体轰动一时的新闻。

sentences.en: Well, he pays up to it, doesn't he?
sentences.zh: 嗯，他很会利用这一点，不是吗？

sentences.en: Of course.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: It's really important.
sentences.zh: 这真的很重要。

sentences.en: Sheridan tends to say to Custer, please don't take too many journalists.
sentences.zh: 谢里丹倾向于对卡斯特说，请不要带太多的记者。

sentences.en: Yeah, he does.
sentences.zh: 没错，他确实这么说了。

sentences.en: And so Custer's response to this is to recruit a few more.
sentences.zh: 而卡斯特对此的回应是又多招募了几个。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, Custer is given so many opportunities by his superiors, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 是啊，我的意思是，卡斯特的上司给了他那么多机会，不是吗？

sentences.en: Sheridan is so tolerant of him.
sentences.zh: 谢里丹对他太宽容了。

sentences.en: Custer keeps letting him down.
sentences.zh: 卡斯特却不断让他失望。

sentences.en: I think it's that quote from Ian Frazier that we had about 20 episodes ago.
sentences.zh: 我想起了大约20集前我们引用的伊恩·弗雷泽的那段话。

sentences.en: I mean, I think it does kind of capture something about it.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我觉得那段话确实捕捉到了某种精髓。

sentences.en: He's fun.
sentences.zh: 他很有趣。

sentences.en: Custer is the kind of embodiment of what these desk-occupying political generals dealing with an industrial army,
sentences.zh: 卡斯特是那些坐在办公室里的政治将军们所向往的化身，他们面对的是一支工业化军队，

sentences.en: you know, as children maybe imagined being a soldier would be like, dashing around on cavalry, leading expeditions, all that kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 你知道，就像孩子们可能想象的那样，当一名士兵会是什么样子：骑着马四处奔波，领导探险队，诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: I think they indulge him because people do sometimes indulge characters, don't they?
sentences.zh: 我想他们纵容他，因为人们有时确实会纵容某些角色，不是吗？

sentences.en: And I think you're absolutely right.
sentences.zh: 我想你是完全正确的。

sentences.en: And he's good for the reputation of the army, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 而且他对军队的声誉很有利，不是吗？

sentences.en: And he's got lots of credit for the Civil War.
sentences.zh: 他在内战中也积累了很多功勋。

sentences.en: And the Civil War, we shouldn't underestimate how important the Civil War is.
sentences.zh: 而且内战，我们不应低估内战的重要性。

sentences.en: The Civil War, arguably the world's first industrial war, seismic, psychological impact.
sentences.zh: 内战，可以说是世界上第一场工业战争，具有地震般的心理冲击。

sentences.en: And if you've got a good war record, as almost all the politicians of these decades do, then that will get you a very long way.
sentences.zh: 如果你有良好的战争记录，就像这几十年来几乎所有的政客一样，那么这会让你走得很远。

sentences.en: And Custer can trade for years on his record in the Civil War.
sentences.zh: 而卡斯特可以凭借他在内战中的记录吃上好几年老本。

sentences.en: Well, but also journalists.
sentences.zh: 嗯，但还有记者们。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So you quote here the young William E.
sentences.zh: 所以你在这里引用了年轻的威廉·E·柯蒂斯的话，

sentences.en: Curtis, who writes of Custer, he's a great man, a noble man is General Custer.
sentences.zh: 他写道：卡斯特是一位伟人，卡斯特将军是一位高尚的人。

sentences.en: I mean, he's not a general, is he?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他不是将军，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, that's important to say.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这一点很重要。

sentences.en: He was a general, but he's now what?
sentences.zh: 他曾经是将军，但现在是什么？

sentences.en: I think Colonel Lieutenant or something, if that's such a thing.
sentences.zh: 我想是中校之类的，如果真有这个职位的话。

sentences.en: Then there is such a thing as a Colonel Lieutenant.
sentences.zh: 确实有中校这个军衔。

sentences.en: And actually, were this an American podcast, Tom, they would undoubtedly know that detail.
sentences.zh: 而且说实话，汤姆，如果这是一个美国播客，他们肯定会知道这个细节。

sentences.en: They would.
sentences.zh: 他们会的。

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: But he's not a general.
sentences.zh: 但他不是将军。

sentences.en: I mean, that's the salient point.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是重点。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: His wife, a charming lady who has shared his marches and victories since early in the war, is as gentle and cultivated, and yet as soldierly as a woman can be.
sentences.zh: 他的妻子，一位迷人的女士，自战争初期就一直陪伴着他的行军和胜利，她既温柔又有教养，却又像女人所能做到的那样具有军人气质。

sentences.en: I mean, it's so like buckets of syrup being poured over Custer.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这就像往卡斯特身上泼了一大桶糖浆一样。

sentences.en: That same guy who's from the Chicago inter-ocean, and he also reports for the New York world, he said, one day I went in to find Custer, and he was with two little girls,
sentences.zh: 那个来自《芝加哥环球报》的家伙，他也为《纽约世界报》报道，他说，有一天我进去找卡斯特，他正和两个小女孩在一起，

sentences.en: one white and one black, teaching them to read.
sentences.zh: 一个白人女孩，一个黑人女孩，教她们读书。

sentences.en: Oh.
sentences.zh: 哦。

sentences.en: And it's just such an unbelievably implausible, clearly untrue story.
sentences.zh: 这简直是一个令人难以置信、显然不真实的故事。

sentences.en: But also, I mean, Custer, he gives good copy.
sentences.zh: 但同时，我的意思是，卡斯特，他提供了很好的素材。

sentences.en: He does.
sentences.zh: 他确实提供了。

sentences.en: So when he rides off on the Black Hills expedition, he takes a band.
sentences.zh: 所以当他骑马去黑山探险时，他带了一支乐队。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: They kind of canter off playing Gary Owen.
sentences.zh: 他们一边演奏着《加里·欧文》一边小跑着出发。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And every morning when they break camp, the band serenades the troops to get them in a kind of marching spirit.
sentences.zh: 每天早上他们拆营时，乐队都会为部队演奏小夜曲，让他们有一种行军的精神。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: He loves all that stuff, doesn't he?
sentences.zh: 他喜欢所有这些东西，不是吗？

sentences.en: Very Walter Scott.
sentences.zh: 非常有沃尔特·司各特的风格。

sentences.en: Calamity Jane is there.
